newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles mostly lower with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles mostly lower with cash.

text.p: The NYMEX electricity complex settled mostly lower Thursday in line with weaker cash market prices due to warmer temperatures and more generating capacity returning to the western U.S.
"Technically, we were due for a correction," said one Northwest futures trader.

May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures ended down 10 cents at $11.10 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $10.90 and $11.15. June COB finished down 11 cents at $11.39. Other COB months settled 10 to 15 cents lower.
May Palo Verde (PV) ended up 10 cents at $15.14 after posting a low of $14.90. June PV finished down 21 cents at $16.41. July and August PV settled up two cents and down six cents, respectively.
The power contracts were buoyant in recent sessions by cooler-than-normal spring conditions and unexpected outage of the Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit.
The 1,073 MW Diablo Canyon unit 2 on the coast of central California remained in "hot standby" mode after being taken off line last Saturday to repair a feedwater pump line.
The loss of Diablo Canyon 2 is offset by returns of the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 3 nuclear power unit in Arizona and the 1,070 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California.
Day-ahead firm, peak electricity prices at COB fell to $12.75-13.25 a megawatt hour (MWh) from yesterday's $14.00-15.00, while those at PV slipped $1 to $15.00-16.00.
Market sources expect the complex to test today's low again as the market's mood turned more bearish.
"It's due for more weakness," said the Northwest trader.
Separately, the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada was shut last Saturday for planned maintenance and was expected to stay down until May 11.
A 750 MW unit at the Navajo coal-fired plant in Arizona was heard still idled for repairs, which could take as long as two weeks to resume production.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington was idled last Thursday for maintenance into the summer.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average about six degrees Fahrenheit below normal through Friday, with little precipitation expected with the exception of the northern Rockies and the extreme Northwest.

In the Southwest, forecasts called for temperatures about six degrees below normal in the southeast and near normal in the northwest for the next couple of days. Southern sections were expected to have several more days of unsettled weather.
NYMEX estimated 391 COB and 435 PV contracts were sold, more than 357 COB and 303 PV lots yesterday.
